correctness.rationale: For each coupon, rate-one Poissonization turns age>L into marked long-gap absence intervals. A bounded time interval contains at most one start per coupon, with probability lambda|I|/n and independent Exp(1) overshoot, yielding a marked Poisson superposition and stationary immigration-death limit. Global Poisson-clock fluctuations on O(n log n) events are o(n^-1/3); near-threshold geometric gaps have expected count O(n^-1/3 log n), allowing a J1 transfer to fixed-draw windows. Zero visits have positive holding intervals, so first hitting times converge. The stationary resolvent convolution gives the claimed Laplace transform. Actual verify.py passed 186 finite-identity/consistency assertions; these are not substitutes for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: At the natural critical window, Long’s stationary mass/flux does not specify time correlations or first stationary completion. The theorem identifies the entire dynamical scaling limit, decay correlations, and the exact nonexponential stationary first-completion distribution. It also makes the cross-model universality to the clumsy coupon queue mathematically explicit, with a proof that handles deterministic expiration rather than random independent refresh.
